title: Load signal correlator and investigation playbook for tokens/sec/p95 regressions
creator: Marcus Patel
description: Build a correlated investigation flow that ties benchmark result storage (tokens/sec, p95 latency, error rates) to an interactive comparison UI and an automated triage playbook. Goals: 1) capture fully qualified run metadata and lineage (commit, model-variant, seq-dist, hardware SKU, batching config), 2) provide fast pairwise and cohort diffs with statistical significance hints, 3) attach automated root-cause signals (hardware throttling events, kernel selection changes, cache hit-rate deltas), and 4) create a repeatable investigation runbook that surfaces prioritized next steps and auto-annotates evidence into the benchmark record.
comments: 2025-02-18 Marcus Patel: Ticket opened after oncall reported unexplained p95 regressions in canary. Initial hypothesis: kernel selector fallback after quantization change causing CPU spillover. Action: persist full runtime metadata on every run.

2025-02-20 Ava Chen: Spike completed for result schema. Decided to include 'sequence_length_histogram' and 'kv_cache_hit_rate' in top-level metadata to make diffs cheaper. Draft schema pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prs/12481
2025-02-22 Samira Iqbal (SRE): Observability hook proposed to pipe GPU telemetry (power/clock throttles) into bench events. Needs RBAC scope for telemetry API. Marked as dependency ENG-58210.

2025-02-25 Design review (Lukas Meyer): Mockup feedback: show 'confidence band' on p95 comparisons and allow locking baseline run. UI should surface sample size and significance test used. Design doc updated: see attachments.

2025-02-27 QA (Diego Ramos): Synthetic regression reproduction: 18% tokens/sec drop when batch_size=64 with specific kernel path. Repro steps added to record and attached to benchmark event. Suggest auto-tagging run with 'kernel-path-regressed'.

2025-03-01 Marcus Patel: Implemented triage automations: when p95 increases >10% and tokens/sec decreases >8% versus baseline, create a 'bench-investigation' object with top 3 suspect signals (kernel_change, cache_hit_delta, infra_throttle). Pushed a prototype workflow runner to infra: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prs/12512

2025-03-02 PM feedback (Rina Gupta): PM asks to add a customer-impact label mapping (none|low|medium|high) that maps from weighted metrics and customer routes affected. Added to plan; mapping doc is in Confluence.

2025-03-03 Ava Chen: Integration test failures flapping on CI due to mock telemetry timeouts. Working with SRE to add retry/backoff. Next: add UI story for annotating evidence bundles and linking GitHub PRs/Runbooks.
notes: Design decisions: prefer append-only run records to keep immutable evidence bundles. Diffs computed at query-time using precomputed aggregates to avoid full-scan comparisons.
Storage trade-off: keep full token-level trace for failing runs only (configurable TTL 30 days) and aggregated histograms for all runs (retention 1 year).
Alerting: new regression alert rule implemented in AlertManager that triggers bench-investigation creation and posts to #bench-regressions with a link to the comparison canvas.
UI behavior: pairwise view with statistical test (Welch's t + bootstrap CI) plus cohort view that shows distribution shifts across seq-length buckets.
Next steps: stabilize telemetry ingestion (ENG-58210), finish UI annotations (DES-4124), add e2e replay harness for suspected regressions (ENG-58055).
